newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: TEJ roars higher on restructuring move.
newsitem.headline: TEJ roars higher on restructuring move.

text.p: Shares in South African clothing firm Towles, Edgar Jacobs Ltd (TEJ) rose sharply on Tuesday as players digested news that it was to sell a large stake in its operations and get new controlling shareholders.

By about 0840 GMT TEJ, which is to be bought by new Western Cape-based investment group Capestar Growth Investments, had jumped 100 percent to a new year high of 600 cents, making it the highest percentage gainer on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.
But volumes traded on the counter were small with only 4,000 shares worth around 19,500 rand changing hands.
"I know there's a big announcement from the company today about a buy-out and an offer to minorities and I think that's basically why the share price is moving there," one dealer said.
He added that: "Most people think this (restructuring move) will be positive because the company was not doing a lot."

TEJ said late on Monday that it planned to sell its clothing operations as a going concern to subsidiary Enteeb Investments (Proprietary) Ltd, in which CapeStar will hold 60 percent with the balance being held by management.

TEJ consists of a consortium of investors led by former Massmart director Michael Rubin, Capital Partners and Fedsure Asset Management which paid eight million rand for 44 percent of TEJ's issued ordinary share capital, including 1.1 million previously held by the Jacobs family.

Rubin told a news briefing CapeStar planned to target investments of a minimum of two million rand in projects in tourism, agribusiness, the expansion of export led manufacturing, local media and property and financial services.
TEJ would then will be listed as CapeStar in the investments trusts sector on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, he added.
Rubin expected CapeStar to make between four and six investments over the next 12 months as well as launch a rights offer.
